headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Devin↔Dify shared integrations and writable workspaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, MCP, Slack, GitHub, and browser content in a cloud workspace, while Dify can wire tools into agent/workflow apps and consume uploaded knowledge base files. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from one side is treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Devin reads Dify-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
IF Dify ingests Devin-generated content into an agent prompt or tool chain
mitigations: Add explicit provenance tags to all cross-agent text
Block instruction-following from uploaded or shared content
Review one sample workflow for prompt-injection handling
Restrict shared channels to structured JSON only
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and allowlists at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion. Dify handles knowledge-base files, conversation logs, and model-provider/tool credentials. A shared workspace or integration can move sensitive data between them in default configurations, but the blast radius is bounded by the documented surfaces rather than uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF Devin forwards repo or chat content into a Dify workflow
IF Dify stores Devin-originated secrets in conversation logs or KB files
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared inputs
Disable logging for sensitive workflows
Use separate projects/workspaces for each agent
Rotate any credentials exposed in test runs
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shells, and Devin also modifies git state while Dify runs server-side Python code in a sandbox container. If they target the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the safer reading is high severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo or directory
IF Devin commits while Dify edits the same files without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write access with a simple manual lock
Pause one agent during git operations
Review pending diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act inside its workspace, and Dify can route agent/workflow outputs into tools. If Dify treats Devin output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or commits. Because Dify also supports user-defined tools and Devin is autonomous, the pathway exists in default-style setups, though verification steps could reduce impact.
conditions: IF Dify passes Devin output directly into a tool or workflow step
IF Devin-generated facts are used without a verification gate
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require structured outputs with schema checks
Compare Devin claims against source artifacts
Limit Dify tools to read-only during testing
requires-engineering: add automated verification before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Dify stores conversation logs and knowledge-base content and may use model-provider APIs. If regulated or sensitive data flows from Devin into Dify, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated data from Devin is copied into Dify conversation logs
IF Dify retention exceeds the source-system retention policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Set short retention on Dify logs
Document data-flow boundaries
Delete test conversations after validation
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
